notes: Spread JACK IN infrastructure farther from the operator and reduced relay footprint for more negative space
Added Quickhack rule parsing for save ability, damage formula/type, half-on-success, lingering/timed damage, conditional requirements, and secondary-target warnings
Target saving throws now use the target actor's real D&D5e ability score, save proficiency, proficiency bonus, and numeric save bonuses
RUN now spends RAM then opens an in-JACK-IN Quickhack Resolution screen instead of only posting chat
Resolution screen shows actual d20 save roll, modifier, total, DC, pass/fail margin, effect state, and source effect text
Damage Quickhacks roll their actual damage formula and prefill a suggested application amount based on save outcome
Half-on-success damage is automatically suggested at half; successful negating saves suggest zero damage
Lingering-save patterns such as Overheat keep primary damage separate from the save and visibly flag lingering adjudication
Conditional and splash/secondary-target Quickhacks are visibly flagged instead of being falsely auto-resolved
Damage application consumes temporary HP first, then HP, and updates the target actor directly when the user has permission
Damage resolution stays bound to the originally Quickhacked token even if Foundry target selection changes while the panel is open
Resolved HP is updated live in the resolution panel and duplicate application is prevented
Static gate passed: V3 JS parses cleanly and Cyberdeck V3 CSS is structurally balanced
knownManualRules: Status conditions and non-damage secondary effects are resolved and displayed but not yet converted into Foundry Active Effects
Conditional requirements such as explosive possession, cybernetic/electronic eligibility, or nearby secondary targets still require GM confirmation
Timed damage such as Overheat is rolled and surfaced but the timing of later-round application remains manual
Quickhack rules are currently parsed from canonical effectText; a future catalog migration should move save/damage/effect metadata into explicit flags
